title: Streamlined quant execution planner + compact dequant adapter for token-aware KV scheduling
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Improves INT8/FP8 serving throughput by introducing an execution planner that reduces kernel switch overhead and a compact dequant adapter that lowers memory traffic for KV-heavy workloads. No API changes.
description:
Summary: This PR implements an execution planner (opPlanner) that consolidates token-aware scheduling decisions for quantized execution and adds a compact dequant adapter to reduce memory bandwidth when materializing per-head dequant scales during KV access.

Motivation: We observed a ~10-18% latency tail increase on inference traces with highly variable prefix lengths (chat workloads) due to frequent kernel rebinds and repeated per-token dequantization of KV slices. The execution planner centralizes kernel selection and microbatch coalescing decisions so we can: 1) avoid unnecessary kernel swaps between INT8 and FP8 execution paths, 2) perform token-aware microbatching (coalesce short requests without increasing worst-case p99), and 3) opportunistically reuse dequantized KV tiles across nearby requests.

Key changes (implementation):
- runtime/op_planner/: new planner that consumes request metadata (sequence length, preferred precision, routing hints) and emits an execution plan (kernel sequence, batch boundaries, cache reuse hints). The planner is intentionally lightweight and deterministic.
- runtime/kv/compact_dequant_adapter.cc/.h: implements a contiguous short-lived dequant buffer format for KV tiles (packed per-head) and a fast path that returns zero-copy views when the backend supports in-place requantization.
- runtime/scheduler/token_coalescer: token-aware microbatch coalescer that groups short sequences up to a configurable token_budget without violating per-request latency SLO.
- runtime/kernels/int8_fp8_router: refactor to accept planner directives (prefer_packed_dequant, pipeline_stage) rather than making per-call heuristics.
- tests/e2e/quant_scheduling: added synthetic traces (mixed chat, streaming) to validate fallbacks, drift metrics, and throughput comparisons.

Behavioral notes:
- New planner adds a small scheduling decision cost (~100ns/request) but reduces kernel boundary crossings by ~45% on our workloads.
- Compact dequant adapter reduces memory traffic on KV reads by up to 28% (measured on A10 tests) and shows a 6-12% end-to-end token throughput gain for chat workloads that frequently hit regional KV reuse.
- FP8 fallback profile: planner can downgrade to FP8 when batch composition indicates reduced head-wise variance; this is a conservative fallback and requires explicit policy in model profile.

Review conversation (condensed into single thread):
- Miguel Santos (requested changes 2026-02-21): "Can we avoid introducing a new planner API surface that duplicates existing scheduler logic? Please sketch migration path and ensure we don't regress dedicated capacity flow."
- Asha Menon (author reply 2026-02-22): "Planned migration: op_planner is a thin layer that currently delegates to the old heuristics for Dedicated. We'll keep a feature flag and run against Dedicated smoke tests; the planner only becomes authoritative after a canary window. Added tests to assert identical decisions for dedicated ./config/dedicated_mode=true."
- Priya Rao (comment 2026-02-24): "Bench numbers look good, but please add a synthetic with heavy KV churn and one with nearly zero reuse to validate worst-case."
- Asha Menon (author reply 2026-02-25): "Added two e2e traces per request type and added guardrail metrics for KV-churn p99. Also instrumented planner decision latency."
- Jordan Kim (approved 2026-02-28): "Approach looks reasonable; compact_dequant_adapter is neat and the allocator is safe on our backends. Approving for merge once CI green."

CI and gating:
- CI: linters + unit tests + integration tests passed.
- Perf job: ran mixed_chat on A10/4xGPU with committed harness; throughput improved 9.8% median and 7.3% p99 improvement over baseline.
- A flakey GPU test failed initially (cuda-allocator-timeout) and was rerun; final run green.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-gate op_planner behind runtime flag (runtime.feature_flags.op_planner).
- Canary 5% traffic on main for 48h with perf/latency alarms.
- If regressions within 48h, auto-fallback to legacy heuristics.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main (squash commit: "quant: add execution planner + compact dequant adapter (ENG-1248)").

Notes for ops:
- docs/ops/quant-deploy.md contains rollout steps, guardrail alert thresholds and suggested KMS settings for private deployments.

Follow-ups (next steps):
- Investigate cross-request dequant tile sharing (requires KV stability guarantees).
- Add more aggressive FP8 autotuner based on live head-variance signals.
- Add telemetry to track planner-induced kernel-switch reductions per model.
